blocks.text: ILIGAN CITY — The national government-run Amai Pakpak Medical Center (APMC) in Marawi City has encouraged at-risk individuals to undergo HIV screening as the number of confirmed cases treated through its AIDS treatment hub surged to 232 from 2022 up to recently Dr. Monerah Luzviminda Macud, a medical specialist at APMC, said the hospital remains open to individuals who want to be screened for Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV). APMC began serving as an AIDS treatment hub in 2020, but its services were temporarily suspended before resuming in 2022, Macud said.
